summary: This paper establishes definitive structural, quantitative, and number-theoretic optimality across all three stages of the recent 37-year breakthrough proving Pinwheel Scheduling PSPACE-completeness (Fotakis et al., 2026). First, in Stage 1, the authors prove that strip high hour H=5 and gap g=3 are exact minimums, compressing daily width to w=60N+13 and calendar period to M=8m+8 (a 16.7% linear reduction cascading as (5/6)^4 approx 0.482 into the Stage 2 job count), and construct an optimal 4-day write phase cutting overhead by 75% while proving unconditional lower bound L >= 4. Second, in Stage 2, they prove a universal number-theoretic lower bound: any pairwise-coprimality witness gadget with chi(G) >= 3 and omega(G) <= 2 requires at least 5 distinct primes (K >= 2310), and solve the exact filler-minimization problem to prove (6,10,55,77,21) is the unique global optimum with 3822 rigid fillers (saving 180 jobs per test over Fotakis et al.). Third, in Stage 3, they sharpen density-slack bounds to the moving-job rate S_2 and prove an exact per-job total-variation cut theorem reducing the soundness day-length threshold from T > n(2E+3) to T >= E+1, saving >2n in the cut step. All 18 core algebraic theorems are formally verified in Lean 4.35.0 with zero sorries and zero custom axioms, backed by zero-float SHA-256 certificates.
